text:
maya: Heads up — planning a weighted shift tonight in the US‑WEST change window (23:00‑01:00 UTC). Goal: send ~30% traffic to v2 (no schema changes). I'll do gradual weights with routerctl and pin session affinity. Will announce preflight 15m prior.

raul: SGTM. Any post-deploy smoke checks we should run? Also which circuit for drain?

sophia: Are we pinning by cookie or header? Cookie TTL will affect sticky sessions for web clients.

maya: We'll pin by router version header + set cookie fallback. TTL 30m. Router commands (preflight):
```
routerctl set-weight service-llm-us-west v2=0.1 v1=0.9
routerctl set-affinity service-llm-us-west method=version header=x-service-version cookie_ttl=1800
```
I'll ramp: 10% -> 30% over ~10m if healthchecks pass.

ops-oncall: Update runbook with rollback criteria pls. I'll be watching p50/p95, error-rate, and backend mem spikes.

maya: Rollback criteria I'm proposing:
- p95 latency > 300ms sustained > 5m
- error-rate delta > +1.0% vs baseline for 5m
- new OOMs or recurring 5xx from v2 hostgroup
Rollback action: immediate weight cut to 0 for v2 + start draining v2 hosts, fallback to v1. Notify customers if >30m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: [23:00:00 UTC] scheduled shift job queued by maya. Canary healthchecks pending.

sophia: How do we validate KV cache warm/kv hits for v2? We should avoid cold-start p95 spikes.

maya: Quick validation commands:
```
curl -H "x-service-version: v2" https://canary.us-west.internal/health
# check cache hits in observability: `llm.kv.cache.hit_rate{env:us-west,version:v2}`
```
I'll warm cache by replaying representative prefixes for 10m pre-shift.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: [23:05:10 UTC] canary checks PASS: 1m p95=120ms, errors=0.2% :white_check_mark:

ops-oncall: I'll take watch. If p95 > 300ms or errors spike, I'll call the rollback and post timeline. @maya ping me when starting the 10% step.

maya: Starting ramp at 23:00 UTC, step1 -> 10% now, will report back after 5m with metrics. :rocket:

raul: :thumbsup: keep the thread updated. Thanks team.
